name: Try You
summary: Shopify app that adds an AI virtual try-on button to product pages: shoppers upload a photo and see themselves wearing the item, with no monthly fee and usage billed per successful try-on through Shopify.
best_for: Shopify stores selling clothing, eyewear, bags, shoes or accessories that want shoppers to see the item on themselves, and prefer paying per use over a fixed monthly app fee
skip_if: your theme is not Online Store 2.0, your margins cannot carry a per-try-on charge on heavy traffic, or you cannot have shopper photos processed by third-party AI models outside the EU
honest_knock: The cost scales with use, not with sales: every successful try-on is billed, from $0.04 to $0.58 depending on quality, so a busy button on cheap products can cost more than it earns, and the volume-discount thresholds are not published. Shopper selfies go to Google or OpenAI, and as a fallback to ByteDance/BytePlus in Singapore, which matters if your shoppers are in the EU. The app asks for edit access to customers and 60 days of order history. It is young: listed since 13 May 2026, by Swicelso OÜ in Estonia.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Light · per usage, per successful try-on, no monthly fee
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-24 on the Shopify App Store listing apps.shopify.com/tryyou, the vendor site tryyou.fly.dev, its terms and its privacy policy) Free to install with 10 free try-ons, then pay per successful try-on with no monthly subscription. The price depends on the quality level you pick: Light $0.04 (1024 × 1536), Medium $0.12, Pro $0.19 (1024 × 1536), HD $0.37 and Ultra $0.58 (1536 × 2048, 2K). The vendor's own example: 100 try-ons cost about $4 on Light and $19 on Pro. Volume discounts go up to 50% off, down to $0.02 per try-on, but the thresholds are not published. You set a monthly spending cap between $5 and $10,000; failed try-ons are never billed; all charges go on your Shopify invoice in USD, and the terms say prices exclude tax. Uninstalling stops billing. Re-read on 14 November 2026 with a plain fetch of the Shopify App Store listing and tryyou.fly.dev: $0.04 to $0.58 per successful try-on by quality level (Light $0.04, Medium $0.12, Pro $0.19, HD $0.37, Ultra $0.58), first 10 free, volume discount down to $0.02, a monthly cap between $5 and $10,000, billed in USD through Shopify. Unchanged.

schema_offer.description: Light, per successful try-on, no monthly fee; Light $0.04, Medium $0.12, Pro $0.19, HD $0.37, Ultra $0.58; first 10 free; volume discount up to 50%, down to $0.02; monthly spending cap $5-$10,000; failed try-ons not billed; billed in USD through Shopify, prices exclude tax. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-14.

compare_with.name: A size guide and model photos
compare_with.why: The alternative most stores already have is a good size guide plus photos of the item on models of different builds, which costs nothing per view. Try You adds a picture of the shopper themselves, at $0.04 to $0.58 per try-on (read 24 October 2026). Its own analytics attribute orders to try-ons, so after a few weeks you can see whether that beats what the photos alone were doing.

claims.claim: Turn your product pages into fitting rooms.
claims.observed: The welcome screen and the onboarding show five models and sample photos, but no try-on was made, because it needs a photo of a person and we use none, so no fitting result was seen.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Welcome screen wording versus a core action that was not run for lack of a person photo.
claims.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about whether a shopper sees a good fitting result on a product page.

claims.claim: In 30 seconds, your customer uploads a selfie and sees themselves wearing your product.
claims.observed: No selfie was uploaded and no try-on was made, so neither the time nor the result of a shopper could be seen.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Welcome screen time claim versus a try-on that was not run.
claims.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about the time a shopper waits or about the look of the result.

claims.observed: Your volume tiers in the settings show Starter at full price for 0 to 499 try-ons a month, then -15%, -30%, -40% and -50% from 10,000 a month. The dossier says the thresholds are not published; the app shows them.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier remark that thresholds are not published versus the volume tiers in the app settings.
claims.buying_consequence: The steps of the volume discount can be read in the app, so the price at your volume can be worked out before you use it.

claims.observed: The settings list Multi-Image Context and Intelligent AI verification at +$0.01 a try-on each, and the dossier names no such extra charges.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier list of charges versus option prices in the app settings.
claims.buying_consequence: Each option adds a cent to the price of every try-on, which is a quarter of the Light price of $0.04.

claims.claim: at a flat $0.08 instead of the level price
claims.observed: The Sensitive-content fallback is switched on by default and bills a flat $0.08 when it recovers a try-on that the main AI refused, which is twice the Light price of $0.04; the dossier does not mention it.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Dossier list of charges versus a default option with a flat price in the app settings.
claims.buying_consequence: A default setting can raise the price of a try-on to $0.08 for explicit looking items such as swimwear or lingerie.

claims.claim: With $10/month on Light, up to ~250 try-ons.
claims.observed: The onboarding says that a cap of $10 a month on Light gives up to about 250 try-ons; at $0.04 a try-on in the settings that is 250.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Onboarding estimate versus the Light price in the settings, without extra options.
claims.buying_consequence: The Light price of $0.04 and the estimate of 250 try-ons for $10 agree, before the optional extras.

claims.claim: You will not be billed for this test charge.
claims.observed: The Shopify approval screen says You will not be billed for this test charge., asks for no card and has an Approve button that could be clicked; it was approved at about 15:09 and nothing was billed.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Approval screen test charge wording versus the approval that was done without a card.
claims.buying_consequence: The app can be activated without a card, and charges start only when a try-on is made.

claims.claim: to a maximum of $10,00 USD per 30 days
claims.observed: The Shopify approval screen shows a usage plan with an app spending limit of a maximum of $10,00 USD per 30 days and no fixed amount; the onboarding cap of $10 matches it, and nothing was used.
claims.plan: Usage plan TryYou: pay per try-on, test charge approved without a card, development store
claims.comparability: Onboarding cap versus the approval screen limit; no stored cost rule was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: You pay per try-on and never more than the cap, which is $10 per 30 days by default; there is no fixed fee.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Try You on a Shopify development store. The core action, a virtual try-on, was not run, because it needs a photo of a person and we deliberately use no photos of real people. Seen were the install permissions, the two-step onboarding with five models and a safety cap, the Playground screen, the Shopify approval screen with a test charge that was approved without a card (billed 0 dollars), the prices per try-on, the options and the volume tiers, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English) showed the button Install and a rating of 5.0 from 5 reviews. The Install app dialog in the admin asked for View customer data (Device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View store data (Products, orders, store analytics). The install was approved at about 15:05 and at 15:06 the app was open on its welcome screen with the texts $0 today, free to install, Turn your product pages into fitting rooms. and In 30 seconds, your customer uploads a selfie and sees themselves wearing your product. Onboarding: step 2, Pick your model, then put it to the test., shows 10 free credits and five models: Light 1 credit, Medium 1 credit, Pro 1 credit, High 2 credits and Ultra 2K 3 credits, five sample person photos of the app and the auto-detected test product The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard. Step 3, Set your safety limit., says You pay nothing today and that the cap is the limit of the shop and not an amount that is charged, with a standard cap of $10 a month, which on Light means up to about 250 try-ons, and the line that the price drops up to 50% at volume. Core action NOT DONE: the virtual try-on needs a photo of a person (in the Playground 2. Person photo, with Samples or Upload, and in the onboarding a Sample photo). We deliberately use no photos of real people and no real faces, so this step was skipped and the button Generate the try-on was not pressed. No result image was made, so there is no time to a first result and no judgement on the quality, the speed or whether a snowboard is a fitting item. Showing the button in the shop (the block Add to theme) was also not tried, so that no theme change was saved. What was seen: the Playground with You have 10 free tests remaining out of 10., 1. Product to test (My catalog or Custom upload), 2. Person photo and 3. Configuration with Compare 2 configs side by side. Checkout: Activate TryYou ($0 today) opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen with the notice You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan TryYou: pay per try-on, This app bills you for usage charges, and the App spending limit (to a maximum of $10,00 USD per 30 days), with Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. An optional row Add payment method stood on the screen, no card had to be entered and Approve could be clicked. Because the screen says it is a test charge, the test charge was approved at about 15:09 without a card; nothing was billed. There is one plan, so this is the cheapest. After the approval the app said You are live and Welcome aboard! with 10 free credits left in the Playground and three display options (Classic button, Floating badge, Carousel slide). Prices in Settings, Quality and pricing (Light selected): Light $0.04, Medium $0.12, Pro $0.19, High $0.37 and Ultra 2K $0.58 per try-on. Options: Multi-Image Context (+$0.01 / try-on), Intelligent AI verification (+$0.01 / try-on), which starts a second generation billed at the selected model rate when the AI sees a major error, and Sensitive-content fallback, which was switched ON by default: it retries with a backup model when the main AI refuses a try-on it judges too explicit and is billed at a flat $0.08 instead of the level price. Your volume tiers: Starter full price (0 to 499 a month), Growth -15% (500 to 1,999), Scale -30% (2,000 to 4,999), Pro -40% (5,000 to 9,999) and Enterprise -50% (10,000+). Raising the monthly cap needs a fresh Shopify approval and lowering it takes effect right away. Deviations from the dossier: the volume thresholds ARE published in the app (the dossier says they are not published). The dossier does not name the extra charges of $0.01 a try-on for Multi-Image Context and for AI verification, nor the $0.08 of the fallback that is on by default. Cancelling: the usage plan has no subscription fee and nothing was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (the Uninstall button stays grey until one is chosen) and there is a feedback box of 250 characters. There is no cancellation fee or waiting time. The reason Testing multiple apps was given at about 15:16 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: generating a try-on (it needs a photo of a person), so the quality, the speed and the cost per result, the storefront blocks and the capture of e-mail addresses (Klaviyo, Shopify Customers), where the selfies go (the privacy policy names AI providers; this was not checked in the app), and the analytics and the CSV export. Clean up: the test charge approval was the only change; the spending cap stayed at $10 as set by the app on activation; no theme change was saved; the app was uninstalled; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Shopify approval screen asks for no card but says only that this is a test charge, while the cap of $10 sits in the plan; a Sensitive-content fallback that costs $0.08 a try-on is switched on by default; two options add $0.01 a try-on; raising the cap needs a new Shopify approval; and the dossier says the volume thresholds are not published while the app shows them.
